title: Rights and responsibilities
examples: What is the difference between a right and a privilege?
Can my rights conflict with someone else's rights?
Does having rights mean I don't have any responsibilities?

explain.say: Today we explore rights and responsibilities in our lives.

items: Rights are things you are entitled to.
Responsibilities are things you must do.

explain.say: Human rights are basic rights for every person.
A duty is a moral or legal obligation we have.
Balancing freedoms means considering others when you act.
When you use a public park, you have the freedom to play.
A common mistake is thinking rights mean no rules at all.

faq.q: Are human rights the same everywhere in the world?
faq.a: Generally, human rights are considered universal standards for all people. However, different cultures or governments might interpret or enforce them differently.
asks: Do all countries accept human rights?
Is there a global agreement on rights?

faq.q: If I have a right, do I also have a duty?
faq.a: Yes, rights and responsibilities are often linked. For example, you have a right to safety, and you have a duty to respect others' safety.
asks: What is the link between rights and duties?

faq.q: Can my freedom stop someone else from exercising theirs?
faq.a: Yes, your freedom ends where another person's rights begin. This is the core of balancing freedoms.
asks: How do I balance my freedom with yours?

faq.q: Are rights something given by a government?
faq.a: No, human rights are considered inherent, meaning they belong to you simply because you are human. Governments must protect them.
asks: Do I need a passport to have rights?
Who gives us our basic rights?

faq.q: What is the difference between a right and a privilege?
faq.a: A right is something fundamental you are entitled to by nature or law. A privilege is something granted to you by someone else, like using a school computer.
asks: Is a right something I earn?

facts: Human rights are considered universal, applying to every person everywhere.
A duty is an obligation, whether moral or legal, that one has towards others.
Balancing freedoms means recognizing that your rights impact others.
The right to life is one of the most fundamental human rights.

quiz.say: If you have the right to free speech, what is a corresponding responsibility?

options.show: You must speak only the truth.
options.say: You must speak only the truth.

options.show: You must not use it to threaten violence.
options.say: You must not use it to threaten violence.

options.show: You must speak all the time.
options.say: You must speak all the time.

quiz.why: The correct answer shows that rights come with limits to protect others.

wrong.0: This is wrong because while truth is valued, the responsibility is about the impact of the speech.
wrong.2: This is wrong because volume does not equal responsible speech.
wrong.3: This is wrong because rights are not absolute and require balance.

quiz.say: If everyone has the right to education, what is a duty of the student?

options.show: To attend classes regularly and study.
options.say: To attend classes regularly and study.

quiz.why: The correct answer shows that rights require active participation and effort.

wrong.0: This is wrong because learning involves making and correcting mistakes.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the primary duty of a student is to learn.
wrong.3: This is wrong because while asking is okay, the duty involves effort when possible.

quiz.say: If you have the right to safety in your home, what is a duty of your family?

options.show: To maintain a safe and caring environment.
options.say: To maintain a safe and caring environment.

options.show: To ignore problems until they get worse.
options.say: To ignore problems until they get worse.

quiz.why: The correct answer reflects the active duty required to uphold another's right.

wrong.0: This is wrong because safety is a shared responsibility within the household.
wrong.2: This is wrong because safety includes emotional and physical care.
wrong.3: This is wrong because a duty requires proactive care and attention.
